dPanel REST API: servers, applications, deployments, modules, load balancers, cloud VMs and executions.
Architecture: docs/architecture/README.md.
info.title: dPanel API

post.description: Sends one message to the assistant. By default the turn streams as Server-Sent Events; with stream set to false it answers with one JSON envelope {conversation_id, title, message, tools, pending_actions}; with async set to true it answers 202 with a turn id to poll at /api/v1/ai/turns/{id}, which avoids proxy response time limits on long turns. Without conversation_id a new conversation is created in the active workspace. The assistant acts only through the dPanel API with the caller's own session and workspace; in this release its tools are read-only. Events: turn.start {conversation_id, title}, message.delta {text}, tool.start {tool_call_id, tool, arguments}, tool.end {tool_call_id, tool, ok}, turn.done {conversation_id, duration_ms}, error {class, message}. Comment lines keep the stream alive.

200.description: JSON when stream is false; otherwise text/event-stream

post.description: Decides one pending action from the caller's own conversation in the active workspace. An approved action runs once, with exactly the arguments recorded when it was proposed, using the caller's session; the assistant then reports the outcome as a new turn. Responds like /api/v1/ai/chat: Server-Sent Events by default, or one JSON envelope with stream set to false. 409 when the action was already decided, has expired, or its conversation is busy.
post.summary: Approve or reject a change the assistant proposed

200.description: JSON when stream is false; otherwise text/event-stream

get.description: Lists the caller's own assistant conversations in the active workspace, most recent first.
Returns one of the caller's conversations in the active workspace with its user and assistant messages. Tool results are not included; assistant messages list the tools they used.

Returns the state of an asynchronous turn started with async set to true, from the caller's own conversation in the active workspace. While status is running, poll again; when completed, result holds the same fields as a JSON chat response; when failed, error holds a safe message.

post.description: Create a new application and its generated workspace IaC playbook. When runtime_items is sent, each item must contain resolved module metadata: real Ansible role names, installer variables, and a stable installation_key. Do not send UI aliases such as roles:["go"]; language runtimes use roles:["dpanel-runtime"] with variables like {"golang_version":"1.24.2","runtime_module":"go","runtime_version":"1.24.2"} and installation_key "go@1.24.2:mise". Leave runtime_items out to let dPanel fill them from setup.language.

post.description: Update application metadata and refresh the generated workspace IaC playbook. The request is merge-style: send only fields that changed. runtime_items must contain selected module metadata with real Ansible role names and resolved variables; do not send UI aliases such as roles:["go"]. Use GET /api/v1/application/{id}/iac to read the current normalized runtime_items before rendering edit forms. bootstrap=true also queues a bootstrap deployment. workdir, app_definition.run.port and app_definition.run.name are fixed once the application exists: repeating the current value is accepted, a different value answers 400.

get.description:
Get one cloud project by ID.
Response user is the identity-backed owner detail. Response workspace is present for group-owned cloud projects. Internal owner_provider and credential data are not returned.

Get cloud project billing accounts in the selected workspace. IDCloudHost returns active, non-deleted billing account choices for VM creation; server/create can auto-select a billing account when vm.billing_account_id is omitted.
Get cloud project provider keypair choices in the selected workspace. Biznet Gio NEO Lite uses the selected dPanel SSH key by default; provider keypair_id is an optional fallback.

Scan the cloud project's provider for VMs dPanel created that have no server record (machine plus cloud_virtual_machines row). A VM counts as dPanel-created when tagged managed-by=dpanel (its workspace tags must match the selected workspace, or the caller in personal scope), or for older untagged VMs when it uses the dpanel-<name> AWS security group, this project's dpanel-c-<id>-m-<id> GCP network tag, or a dnocs-e2e- or dpanel-e2e- name (DigitalOcean and IDCloudHost VMs carry no dPanel tags, so only those names count there). Untagged VMs without that evidence are never listed. Supports AWS, GCP, DigitalOcean, IDCloudHost and Tencent Cloud. Without region, AWS, Tencent Cloud and IDCloudHost scan every region.

parameters.description: AWS region or GCP region/zone to scan
parameters.name: region

post.description: Queue deletion of one orphan VM of the cloud project. Manager re-scans the provider and only accepts a VM that is still an orphan visible to the caller; confirm must repeat the VM name. AWS deletes by instance ID and removes the dpanel-<name> security group; GCP deletes by name and zone, plus the managed ingress firewall; DigitalOcean, IDCloudHost and Tencent Cloud delete by instance ID. Region is the zone for GCP and the region elsewhere. Poll the returned execution with the orphan executions endpoint.

get.description: Get the status of an orphan VM deletion execution of the cloud project. Orphan deletions have no server, so they are not listed by the machine-scoped execution endpoints.

Get cloud project OS templates in the selected workspace. IDCloudHost returns one normalized item per published plain OS image version, including os_name and os_version for VM creation. Biznet Gio NEO Lite requires product_id query and returns select_os choices. AWS returns realtime AMI choices for the selected region via zone query.

parameters.description: Provider product ID for providers whose OS list depends on product/package selection
parameters.name: product_id

parameters.description: Provider zone/region selector. AWS expects this to be the selected region (for example ap-southeast-1).
parameters.name: zone

parameters.description: Optional search filter for template name, description, or AMI ID. Supports plain text and wildcard patterns (*, ?), for example Ubuntu Server, name=ubuntu*, or ami-1234*.
parameters.name: filter

parameters.description: Optional AWS-only family filter, for example ubuntu, debian, almalinux, windows, redhat, centos, suse, amazon-linux, rocky, oracle-linux.
parameters.name: os_family

parameters.description: Optional AWS-only tier selector. Default is free-tier. Use tier=all to include non-free-tier AMIs.
parameters.name: tier

parameters.description: Optional curated catalog. ubuntu-lts returns one template per supported Ubuntu LTS release (24.04 and 26.04.1) for AWS, GCP, DigitalOcean, IDCloudHost, Alibaba Cloud and Tencent Cloud, labelled for display; other filters are ignored.
parameters.name: catalog

get.description: Get cloud project product/package choices in the selected workspace. Biznet Gio returns NEO Lite products for VM creation with normalized vcpu, ram_mb, disk_gb, default_cycle, and billing_cycles fields. GCP returns machine types for the selected zone with value set to the machine type name, and passes optional filter to the Compute Engine machineTypes API. AWS returns realtime EC2 instance types for the selected region via zone query.

parameters.description: Provider zone for zone-scoped product discovery. Required by GCP machine types and AWS instance type discovery (AWS expects region value).
parameters.name: zone

parameters.description: Product filter. For GCP, provider-native filters such as name=e2* are passed to machineTypes; bare values such as e2- are treated as a machine type name prefix. For AWS instance types, filters support plain text (nano), key=value forms (name=nano*), and wildcard patterns (*, ?).
parameters.name: filter

get.description: Get cloud project regions in the selected workspace. Biznet Gio returns region codes from the provider helper endpoint used for availability choices.

Get the standard VM size form of a cloud project: CPU, memory and disk choices. Flexible providers (IDCloudHost, GCP E2) take any listed CPU and memory pair; fixed providers (AWS, DigitalOcean, Alibaba Cloud, Tencent Cloud) map each pair to the cheapest instance type in stock that fits it, and items lists those types smallest first. Other providers answer mode=catalog and keep their product picker.

parameters.description: Location of the instance catalog: the region for AWS and DigitalOcean, the zone for Alibaba Cloud and Tencent Cloud. Required by fixed providers.
parameters.name: zone

get.description: Get cloud project VPCs/networks in the selected workspace and region. GCP accepts either a region or zone and returns regional subnetworks with id set to the subnetwork selfLink. AWS returns realtime subnet choices for the selected region. Biznet Gio NEO Lite has no customer VPC API; pass product_id to check IP availability and receive the provider-managed default network choice when available.

parameters.description: Filter by region ID, or zone ID for providers such as GCP
parameters.name: region

parameters.description: Biznet Gio NEO Lite product ID used for IP availability checks
parameters.name: product_id

get.description: Get cloud project zones in the selected workspace. GCP returns Compute Engine zones and can filter them with the optional region query. Biznet Gio NEO Lite has no separate zone API, so it returns the provider region codes as zone-compatible choices.

parameters.description: Filter zones by region, for example asia-southeast2

Replace the provider credential of an existing cloud project, for example after rotating a GCP service-account key or an AWS access key. The project ID stays the same, so servers created from it keep working.
Send the full credential object for the project's provider, using the credential fields of its provider contract. dPanel checks the required fields, refuses a GCP credential for a different project_id, and calls the provider with the new credential before storing it encrypted. The credential is never returned.
Requires the cloud-project admin role in a group workspace.

get.description: Clusters of the selected workspace with their derived status. Needs cluster viewer.

post.description: Creates a server group of the cluster's kind with the given servers, stores the cluster and starts its install as one multi-host execution. Servers may have joined over SSH or through the dPanel Agent: when any joined through the agent, the first such server whose agent is online runs the install and reaches the others over their private network with a per-cluster SSH key that each member installs through its own agent (one cluster_access execution per node). Every install first checks that the members reach each other on SSH and the engine's ports; a blocked path fails the cluster with failure_reason and the preflight matrix. Servers must be in this workspace, in no other group, without the dPanel firewall on and without Docker, k3s or RKE2 installed. 409 when no agent-joined member is online. Needs cluster editor and server editor.

get.description: Kinds of cluster a server group can back, with roles, engines and the versions each engine's module lists. Planned kinds are listed with status "planned". Needs cluster viewer.
A cluster with its group, nodes and last execution. Needs cluster viewer.

delete.description: Deletes a cluster that is uninstalled, failed or was never installed. Its server group stays as a generic group with the same members, and members that joined through the agent drop the cluster key (one cluster_revoke execution each). Needs cluster admin and server editor.

post.description: Runs the install again on every node of a cluster whose install failed or that was uninstalled, with the same engine, version, roles and join token, after the same connectivity preflight. Another online agent-joined server takes over when the last one that ran the cluster is offline. Needs cluster editor and server editor.

Removes the engine from every node as one multi-host execution. Servers stay registered and the group keeps its members; when a member ran it, every member then drops the cluster key. Needs cluster editor and server editor.

Move a server, application, domain, load balancer, cloud project or SSH key that you own from your personal workspace into a Casdoor workspace. Once a resource is in a workspace it stays there: moving it to another workspace or back to a personal workspace returns 403. You need editor rights in the target workspace. A resource cannot move away from what it needs (for example a server's SSH key or cloud project) or from what still needs it; set include_dependencies to move the transferable resources it needs along with it. The x-auth-organization-id header does not select the workspace here: source comes from the resource and target from the body.

post.description:
Generates a key pair and stores it encrypted. Send algorithm "ed25519" (the default) or "rsa" with a key_size from /lengths; a payload carrying only key_size is read as RSA. The comment defaults to the signed-in user's email.
This response is the only one that carries the private key, so its owner has to store it now; reads never return it again.

Records a server reached through its agent in the selected workspace and returns a command to run as root on the machine. The command downloads the install script with a single-use enrollment code (valid 2 hours), creates the owner's Linux user and installs the dPanel Agent; the server turns ready when the agent connects. No dnocs sign-in on the machine, public IP, open port or dPanel SSH key is needed. The same per-workspace limit as /api/v1/server/register applies.
post.summary: Get a one-line command that adds a server through the dPanel Agent

post.description: Create a generic dPanel machine over SSH. For a server the user already has, `dnocs machine register` (POST /api/v1/server/register) run on it is the recommended way: no dPanel SSH key is needed. For manual servers, call setup after creation. For cloud-project VM creation (IDCloudHost, Biznet Gio NEO Lite, GCP, AWS, DigitalOcean, Alibaba Cloud or Tencent Cloud), send cloud_project_id/cloud_id, provider, vm and join_method; dPanel IDs such as cloud_project_id, cloud_id, and secret_id must be JSON strings. join_method agent (the default where the provider supports it: IDCloudHost, GCP, AWS, DigitalOcean, Tencent Cloud) installs the dPanel Agent on the VM's first boot: no secret_id, no dPanel key on the VM, and vm.reserve_public_ip may be false (not on DigitalOcean); the server turns ready when the agent enrolls. join_method ssh needs secret_id and a public IP, and queues setup over SSH after provider creation succeeds. Manager stores provider-specific data in cloud_virtual_machines and queues the provider VM playbook. GCP, AWS and DigitalOcean creation return 409 when vm.name is already used by a VM in vm.zone (GCP) or vm.region (AWS, DigitalOcean).

delete.description: soft delete a machine by uninstalling the dPanel agent first; cloud-backed machines queue provider-origin deletion through the worker first; call again after status is deleted to permanently delete the record. A server with deployments, builds or load balancers answers 409 with machineDeleteDependencies; when it is unreachable (its agent silent for 15 minutes, never connected, or SSH failing), can_forget is true and forget=true removes it and those records from dPanel only, stopping its jobs and changing nothing on the machine (docs/features/server-removal.md). A cloud server is forgotten only when its provider says the VM is gone, or, for a provider dPanel cannot ask, with vm_deleted=true; forget never deletes the VM (cloud_vm in the 409 says what the provider answered).

parameters.description: Remove an unreachable server and its records from dPanel only
parameters.name: forget

parameters.description: With forget on a cloud server whose provider dPanel cannot ask: the owner deleted the VM at the provider
parameters.name: vm_deleted

Asks the server's agent for its systemd units and reports, for every installed module that runs a service, whether that service is running. A module whose service is failed, stopped or missing needs attention. checked is false when the agent could not be asked.
For modules whose manifest names the package that carries their release, it also reports the release that is really installed and whether it differs from the one chosen at install (version.mismatch). versions_checked is false when the agent cannot read package versions (agent older than v0.1.30, or a system without dpkg).

get.description: Unfinished executor executions of every workspace, oldest first, with what the executor gateway knows of each: queued or claimed, by which worker, last heartbeat. Each task names who created it (public profile, never email) and a cleanup verdict: safe_to_delete (server deleted, worker silent 10 minutes, out of the queue and silent 30 minutes, or silent 6 hours), stale (unclaimed or silent 15 minutes) or active, with its reasons. Agent requests are left out. Only for the dpanel-admin role.

delete.description: Fails an unfinished execution through the same execution_failed event a worker sends, so its deployment, server, module installation or cloud VM can be retried. When the gateway holds the task, its worker stops at its next heartbeat. Only for the dpanel-admin role.

post.description: Hands an unfinished execution to the next free worker. When the gateway holds it, the current worker's claim is revoked: that worker stops at its next heartbeat (within a minute) and its result is ignored. Otherwise its queue workflow is started again from the original task; this is refused while a worker reported progress in the last 5 minutes. Only for the dpanel-admin role.

Trades a single-use enrollment code for the agent's own credential. Agents that still hold the shared callback token may send it as the bearer token with their machine_id instead, until the shared token is retired. The credential is returned once.

Returns the shell script that creates the owner's Linux user and installs the dPanel Agent for the server an unused enrollment code belongs to (from /api/v1/server/agent-install). The code is sent in the form body and is only used when the agent enrolls. An unknown, used or expired code gets a script that explains it and exits 1.
post.summary: Download the dPanel Agent install script for an enrollment code

get.description: Desired firewall of a server: policy, rules (system rules first, locked), applied version and drift.

put.description: Turn the firewall on or off and set default policies and Docker filtering. Changes take effect on the next apply. version must match the loaded policy.

post.description: Queue a job that converges the server's firewall to the stored policy and rules, installing the firewall module first when needed. version is the policy version the caller reviewed; enable turns a disabled policy on first. The job restores the previous firewall automatically if SSH or the agent stop working. Poll the execution, then read the firewall.
Store the policy as disabled and queue a job that turns ufw off on the server. Rules are kept for the next enable.
Adopt the server's current ufw rules as stored rules so they survive the next apply. legacy stores them as locked legacy rules. Rules dPanel cannot represent are returned as skipped.

get.description: Read the firewall on the server through the agent, with drift against the desired firewall. A server without the firewall module reports available=false and a reason.
Compare the desired firewall with the live one read through the agent: rules to add and remove, foreign rules, policy changes and whether SSH stays open. Changes nothing on the server.

post.description: Store a rule. direction "route" targets a Docker-published container port. Takes effect on the next apply.

delete.description: Delete a stored rule. System and legacy rules are locked. Takes effect on the next apply.

connected.description:
Connected reports whether the account is linked, which is the one thing
a client used the token's presence for.

timeout.description:
Timeout bounds the whole deployment job (clone, runtime setup,
build and service start) as a Go duration such as "90m". Empty
keeps the executor default.

allow_custom.description:
AllowCustom lets a value outside Options through when it matches
Pattern, so a user can pick a release the list does not carry yet.

pattern.description: Pattern is the regular expression every value must match in full.

children.description:
Children are the modules offered under this one, such as the
databases created on a database server. The catalog list nests them
here instead of listing them at the top level.

installed_version.description:
InstalledVersion says where the installed release is read; see
ModuleManifest.InstalledVersion.

parent.description: Parent is set on a child module; see Manifest.Parent.

services.description:
Services are the systemd units the module runs; see
ModuleManifest.Services.

input.description:
Input is the install form input that chose the release, such as
mariadb_use_official_repo_version.

line_parts.description:
LineParts is how many version parts make a release line: 2 for MariaDB
12.3, 1 for PostgreSQL 18.

match.description:
Match is a regular expression a matched package name must also match,
such as ^postgresql-[0-9]+$ (not postgresql-17-postgis-3).

moves.description:
Moves says whether an install may move a server to another release
line: "none" (it keeps the line it runs), "upgrade" (only to a newer
line) or empty (not checked).

package.description:
Package is the Debian package that carries the release, such as
mariadb-server, or a dpkg-query pattern such as postgresql-[0-9]* when
the package name holds the release.

children.description:
Children are the modules offered under this one, such as the
databases created on a database server. The catalog list nests them
here instead of listing them at the top level.

installed_version.description:
InstalledVersion says where the installed release is read; see
ModuleManifest.InstalledVersion.

parent.description: Parent is set on a child module; see Manifest.Parent.

services.description:
Services are the systemd units the module runs; see
ModuleManifest.Services.

runtime.description:
Runtime is where the application's languages come from: "new" (the
new runtime, installed once per server, prebuilt), "previous" (the
previous runtime), or empty to let dPanel decide per server: the
previous runtime where the server already has the version from it, the
new runtime otherwise. It applies at the next bootstrap deploy.

runtime_items.description:
RuntimeItems is the selected module dependency snapshot for generated application IaC.
Each item must carry real Ansible role names and resolved variables from module metadata.

name.description: Name is the build step's own name, set on build_step stages.

file_url.description: can use for github release assets, bucket file, etc

machine_id.description: TODO: should be rename to worker info, can be Machine Group ID, Github Action, Kube Pod, etc

file_url.description: If bucket (s3 / gcs / etc) set, this data will exist

created_at.description: CreatedAt is the provider's image creation time (RFC 3339), when known.

image_name.description: ImageName is the provider's image name when it differs from Name.

preview.description:
Preview marks a provider that is not enabled for the web UI yet but
can be registered and used from the dPanel CLI.

help.example: Maps frontend VM name to the Ansible role VM detail.

rounded_up.description:
RoundedUp is true when the resolved type has more CPU or memory than
requested.

value.description:
Value is the instance type the pair resolves to; empty when the
provider takes CPU and memory as numbers.

configurable.description: Configurable is false when the instance type fixes the disk size.

items.description:
Items lists each distinct instance type the sizes resolve to, smallest
first; it is also the short instance type list for pickers.

disk_gb.description: DiskGB is the disk included with the type, when the type fixes it.

note.description:
Note explains a type whose CPU differs from a plain vCPU count, such
as a shared-core machine.

id.description: ID is the provider instance ID (EC2 instance ID, GCE numeric ID).

network_tags.description: NetworkTags are GCP firewall target tags.

region.description: Region is the region the VM runs in; Zone is set for zonal providers.

security_groups.description: SecurityGroups are AWS security group names attached to the VM.

server_id.description: ServerID is the dPanel server ID from the VM's tags, when tagged.

tags.description: Tags are AWS tags or GCP labels.

ports.description:
Ports are the paths between members the engine needs; the preflight
checks them before every install (docs/hostgroups §4.6).

from.description: From lists the roles that connect; empty means every member.

listen.description: Listen lists the roles that serve the port; empty means every member.

multi_server.description: MultiServer ports matter only with more than one server node.

probe_only.description: ProbeOnly ports are already served (SSH): no test listener.

odd.description:
Odd requires an odd count when more than one node has the role, as
quorum members (etcd) do.

quorum.description: Quorum members must stay in one region (docs/hostgroups §5).

help.example: Provider API token with DNS permissions.

message.example: Provide token or api_key with api_secret.

last_seen_at.description:
LastSeenAt is when the agent last reported to dPanel; absent when it
never has.

reporting.description:
Reporting is dPanel's verdict on LastSeenAt: online (reported within
AgentSilentAfter), silent (quiet longer, possibly restarting), offline
(quiet longer than AgentOfflineAfter: usage, the module list and logs
are stale and the server counts as unreachable) or never.

silent_seconds.description: SilentSeconds is how long the agent has not reported.

upgrade_available.description:
UpgradeAvailable is true when the agent runs an older release than
NewVersion, the release dPanel installs today. An agent that reports
no release tag (an old build) counts as older.

http_port.description: Deprecated: HTTPPort is no longer required. Domain is constructed without it.

join_method.description:
JoinMethod says how a VM dPanel creates in a cloud project joins:
JoinMethodAgent (the default) installs the dPanel Agent on first boot,
JoinMethodSSH runs setup over SSH with the dPanel key of SecretID.

remove_home.description: RemoveHome also deletes the home folder when a Linux user is removed.

service_account_id.description:
ServiceAccountID adds a service account of the server's workspace
instead of the dPanel user in ID; Username and Password are ignored.

cloudflare.description: Only available for domain registered in d-panel and cloudflare DNS.

subdomain.description: Subdomain is the record name under the domain; @ is the root domain.

l4.description: L4 is the listener of an L4 load balancer; empty for L7.

protocol.description: Protocol is http for L7, and tcp or udp for L4.

address_mode.description:
AddressMode says how an application target is reached; see the
AddressMode constants. Ignored without ApplicationID.

database_installation_id.description:
DatabaseInstallationID points an L4 load balancer at an installed
postgresql, mariadb, mongodb or redis module; Manager resolves it to
upstreams with AddressMode.

redirect.description: Redirect is the destination of a rule of type redirect.

resolved_upstreams.description:
ResolvedUpstreams records where an application target was sent the
last time the load balancer was applied, each deployment with its
server's MachineID. Manager sets it; values sent by clients are dropped.

allow_from.description:
AllowFrom lists the IPs and CIDRs that may connect, or ["any"].
Database services must set it.

idle_timeout.description:
IdleTimeout closes a connection with no traffic for this long, as a
Go duration between 1m and 24h; empty means 1h.

listen_address.description:
ListenAddress is 0.0.0.0 or one of the gateway's own addresses; a
private address keeps a database off the public network.

listen_port.description: ListenPort is unique per gateway across L4 load balancers.

service.description: Service is generic, postgresql, mariadb, mongodb or redis.

advance_mode.description: Additional fields for create and update for v2

code.description: Code is 301 or 302; empty means 302, which browsers do not remember.

drop_path.description:
DropPath sends every request to URL itself. By default the requested
path and query are appended to it.

url.description: URL is the destination, http or https, with an optional path.

advance_mode.description: Additional fields for create and update for v2

upstream.description: TODO: Deprecated, will be removed in the future, and use DefaultUpstream instead which is the fallback upstreams

machine_id.description:
MachineID is the server of the application deployment this upstream
was resolved from; only set in Backend.ResolvedUpstreams.

scheme.description:
Scheme is set when the upstream was given as a URL, such as
https://origin.example.com: an origin with its own name. The gateway
then sends the origin's host as Host (and as SNI over https) instead of
the visitor's. Empty means a plain address reached over http with the
visitor's Host, as before.

algorithm.description:
Algorithm picks how the key is generated: "ed25519" (the default) or
"rsa". A payload carrying only KeySize means RSA, which keeps clients
written before Ed25519 support working.

comment.description: Comment labels the public key, normally the owner's email.

last_started_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC; empty when the agent did not report it

restarts.description: automatic restarts systemd counted; nil when the agent did not report it

class.description: Class is active or passive, derived from Type; set on responses.

failure_reason.description:
FailureReason says why the last operation failed: the failed task's
message (a preflight path, an unreachable member, a join that could
not reach the API) or the job error.

preflight.description:
Preflight is the last connectivity check: ok, checked_at, nodes and
one path per node pair and port with its result.

transport.description:
Transport is "worker" (a dPanel worker reaches every member over SSH)
or "member" (ControllerServerID's own worker drives the members with
the cluster key); empty before the first operation of this kind.

ports.description:
Ports are the paths between members the engine needs; the preflight
checks them before every install (docs/hostgroups §4.6).

exclusive.description: Exclusive kinds own their nodes: no other cluster or Docker.

rbac_resource.description:
RBACResource guards the kind: database kinds use "database", the
others "cluster".

access.description:
Access is the node's last cluster access or revoke job, for clusters
driven by a member.

join_method.description: JoinMethod is "agent" or "ssh": how the server joined dPanel.

l4_protocols.description:
L4Protocols are the L4 protocols the engine proxies (tcp, udp); empty
when it serves HTTP load balancers only.

module.description: Module is the server module that installs the engine.

tls.description: TLS is how the engine gets certificates: "builtin" when it runs ACME itself.

total.description: Total is how many lines the whole window holds, when Uptrace reports it.

advance_mode.description: AdvanceMode enables rule/config based load balancer rendering.

config.description: Config is merged with the existing config when present; omitted nested config fields keep their current values.

name.description: Name updates the load balancer display name when present.

rules.description: Rules is a full replacement list when present. Omit rules to keep the current rules; send [] to clear all rules.

runtime_items.description: RuntimeItems selects the load balancer runtime/module. If it contains nginx or caddy/caddyserver, backend updates the engine accordingly.

upstream.description: Upstream updates the legacy default upstream. If omitted and rules has a first upstream address, backend derives this value from rules[0].target.upstreams[0].

total.description: Total is how many lines the whole window holds, when Uptrace reports it.

facts.description: Facts are the type's own details, keyed for the page to label.

owner.description: Owner is who owns the resource, as a public profile (never email).

related.description:
Related are other resources tied to this one, such as the servers an
application is deployed to.

subtitle.description:
Subtitle is a second line under the name, such as an application's
repository.

name.description: Name is the team's name; empty for a personal workspace.

worker_stopped.description:
WorkerStopped is true when the gateway held the task: its worker stops
at its next heartbeat and its result is ignored.

cleanup.description: Cleanup says whether the task is safe to delete, and why.

created_by.description: CreatedBy is who started the task, as a public profile (never email).

server_deleted.description:
ServerDeleted is true when the task names a server that no longer
exists.

action.description:
Action is requeued when the gateway took the task back from its worker
and queued it, or restarted when a new queue workflow was started.

code.description: Code is a single-use enrollment code from a bootstrap script or setup.

machine_id.description:
MachineID is used only by agents migrating from the shared token,
which they send as the bearer token.

secrets.description:
Secrets the action created, such as generated database passwords,
shown to the approving user once. Never stored or given to the model.

Secrets holds the values of the action's secret inputs by name. They
go to the approved action only and are never logged or stored.

async.description:
Async starts the turn in the background and answers 202 with a turn id
to poll at /api/v1/ai/turns/{id}. It takes precedence over stream.

stream.description: Stream selects Server-Sent Events (default) or one JSON response.

secret_inputs.description: SecretInputs are listed while the action is pending.

actions.description:
Actions are the changes this answer proposed, with their current
status, so a client that reopens the conversation can still decide
the ones that are pending.

secret_inputs.description:
SecretInputs are values the user types when approving, passed in
the approval's secrets by name.

actor.description: Actor is who made the request, as a public profile (never email).

region.description: Region is the AWS region or the GCP zone of the VM.

actor.description: Actor is who started the execution, as a public profile (never email).

other.description:
Other counts rows whose status is a legacy or unrecognised value, so
the parts always sum to Total.
Other carries legacy and unrecognised statuses.

has_data.description:
HasData is false when nothing reported, which is a different claim from
every machine reading zero.

machines.description: Machines is how many distinct machines reported anywhere in the window.

peak.description:
Peak names the worst machine per metric across the whole window, so the
chart can say which server to open.

machines.description: Machines is how many machines reported in this bucket.

cloud_vm.description:
CloudVM is what the provider said about a cloud server's VM before
offering to forget it; forget never deletes the VM.

reachability.description:
Reachability and CanForget tell whether the server, being gone, may be
removed with its resources from dPanel only (forget=true).

forgotten.description: Forgotten lists what forget=true removed with the server.

chosen.description: Chosen is the release chosen at install, such as 12.3.

installed.description:
Installed is the release, such as 12.3.3; empty when the package is
not installed.

mismatch.description:
Mismatch is true when the server runs another release than the one
chosen.

missing.description: Missing is true when the package is not installed at all.

package.description: Package is the package the release is read from.

package_version.description:
PackageVersion is the full package version, such as
1:12.3.3+maria~ubu2404.

version.description:
Version is the release the module really runs, when its manifest
names the package that carries it and the agent could read it.

checked.description:
Checked is false when the agent could not be asked (offline, old
agent); the web app then shows the modules without a service state.

versions_checked.description:
VersionsChecked is true when the agent reported the installed package
versions (agent v0.1.30 and newer, Debian and Ubuntu).

include_dependencies.description:
IncludeDependencies also moves the resources this one needs, such as a
server's SSH key and cloud project.

resource_id.description: ResourceID is the dPanel ID of the resource.

resource_type.description:
ResourceType is server, application, domain, load-balancer,
cloud-project or ssh-key.

target.description: Target is "personal" or a Casdoor workspace group ID.

skipped.description: Skipped is true when the agent already runs Version.

upgrade_offered_at.description: UpgradeOfferedAt is when its old agent was last sent agent.upgrade.

workspace_type.description: Workspace fields are filled for administrators only.

owner_linux_user.description:
OwnerLinuxUser is the Linux user setup would create for the person
registering. Setup on a private server reinstalls only the agent, so the
CLI creates it: files and other per-person views look it up by comment.

execution_ids.description:
ExecutionIDs fails exactly these unfinished executions, whatever their
age. When empty, every execution the policy finds stale is failed.

older_than.description: OlderThan replaces the default policy with one age for every class.

remaining.description:
Remaining is true when the batch cap was reached with stale
executions still left; running the cleanup again continues.

resolved.description:
Resolved lists agent requests whose command had already finished: they
get the command's real result instead of a stale failure.

actor.description: Actor is who started the execution, as a public profile (never email).
